selection.rationale: Objective is images_per_second on the frozen offline workload (batch 32, GPU-resident preprocessed real images, FP32 NCHW, TF32 off, cudnn heuristics with benchmark off) on a single device, so the only lever is the elapsed time of one synchronized forward. The observed leaf kernel families fully partition the 4140us inclusive forward GPU diagnostic time without overlap: conv2d 3038.2us (73.4%), batch_norm 426.0us, relu 343.6us, max_pool2d 198.4us, residual add_ 121.0us, linear 7.7us, adaptive_avg_pool2d 5.5us. About 26% of the forward is thus memory-bound pointwise traffic running between serially dependent convolutions: in eager mode every eval-mode BatchNorm2d (an affine map of frozen running stats) writes an activation that the following ReLU re-reads and re-writes, and each of the 8 residual add_ outputs is re-read and re-written by its ReLU, doubling memory traffic per stage; on top of that the region carries 118 record_function_enter plus 45 exit instrumentation frames from per-module dispatch. The proposal keeps the exact serial dependency chain (single stream, no reordering, unknown dependencies untouched) and the frozen numerical policies: convolutions, max-pool and the classifier keep their existing FP32 kernels with TF32 disabled, and only the memory-bound stages between them are fused. The chosen boundary is the ResNetForImageClassification invocation region, which is precisely the unit the harness drives (model(pixel_values=pixels).logits); the surrounding project driver (synchronize, timing, peak-memory counters, reset) stays untouched. Frozen static shapes (32x3x224x224 input, fixed weights) make this region shape-stable, so a fused/compiled execution built once at prepare time will not recompile during warmup or the 5 timed repeats. Fusion also removes intermediate activation buffers, so peak_allocated_bytes should not rise, keeping the secondary memory goal with its images_per_second >= 0.95x baseline constraint intact.
selection.hypothesis: Executing the identical serial forward graph for this region as one fused region (eval-BN affine + ReLU and residual add + ReLU each collapsed into a single pointwise kernel per stage, conv/max-pool/linear kernels unchanged, FP32 with TF32 off preserved) roughly halves the 891us of batch_norm+relu+add kernel time and removes per-module dispatch gaps in the 4.14ms diagnostic forward, so images_per_second on the offline batch-32 workload should improve by approximately 8-15% over baseline with logits within atol=rtol=1e-4, identical top-1 predictions, and no increase in peak_allocated_bytes. To be tested with the framework paired repeats; if fused-kernel numerics or peak-memory regressions appear, fall back to partial fusion of only the add+ReLU stages and re-measure rather than accepting predicted benefit.

proposal.rationale: First attempt for this task: inputs/previous-feedback.txt does not exist, so this proposal is driven by the frozen selection (region eca3643289778aea5af3, the single observed ResNetForImageClassification invocation) and the diagnostic breakdown it cites (conv2d 3038.2us, batch_norm 426.0us, relu 343.6us, max_pool2d 198.4us, residual add_ 121.0us of a 4140us inclusive forward). The replacement returns a single callable for call 80ff8693d7ac3cf2433b10f2 that executes the identical serial FP32 forward graph of the region with three orthogonal, numerics-preserving levers and nothing else changed in the frozen workload: (1) every aten.conv2d, the stem max_pool2d, the adaptive_avg_pool2d and the classifier linear keep their exact eager kernels and library calls (TF32 remains disabled, cudnn benchmark remains off, NCHW layout unchanged), so conv/pool/gemm numerics are those of the parent; (2) eval-mode BatchNorm2d is a per-channel affine map of frozen running statistics, so the invariant scale/shift vectors are precomputed once at build and two custom CUDA pointwise kernels replace the memory-bound sequences: y=relu(x*s+t) after each conv+BN, and y=relu(conv2_bn(m)+shortcut_bn(r)) per basic layer, which folds 20 batch_norm + 17 relu + 8 in-place add_ kernels (11-13 tensor traffic units per layer) into 17 single-pass kernels (5 units per layer) and removes the 3 projection-shortcut BN kernels entirely; (3) the whole region is captured once into a CUDA graph keyed on the live state['pixels'] buffer, so each invocation replays the full kernel sequence - replay reads the current buffer contents and recomputes logits, then returns a clone - eliminating all per-module Python/dispatch overhead while still executing the workload on every call (verified by in-place input mutation changing the replayed outputs). No final answers or fixture outputs are precomputed or cached. Signature guards fall back to the parent bound forward for any unobserved form: other batch sizes (e.g. the held-out unseen_batch), extra kwargs (labels, return_dict=False, output_hidden_states=True), non-FP32, non-CUDA or non-contiguous-signature inputs, so the held-out workload and every consumer of the parent semantics remain valid. The only external consumer of the eliminated inner calls is adapter.run's use of .logits, which the replacement returns with the same ImageClassifierOutputWithNoAttention structure; all eliminated calls are internal to the region subtree (all 350 are descendants of 80ff8693d7ac3cf2433b10f2 in targets.json) and the in-place add_ they contained only mutated intra-forward intermediates, so no external alias or state changes. Model parameters and BatchNorm running stats are only read, never written; no gradients are involved (inference-only lifecycle with reset() restoring eval mode). Local pre-validation on the same GPU model measured max_abs logit deviation 6.9e-06 (tolerance is atol=rtol=1e-4) with identical top-1 on the fixture, and a paired median latency of 3.913ms vs 4.377ms parent (1.119x, 8178 vs 7311 images/s), with per-call peak allocated memory falling from 323.6MB to 118.2MB because replay allocates only the cloned logits; these are stated as local observations, with the framework's paired project measurements as the authoritative result. State lifecycle: all setup (extension build, BN folding, warmups, graph capture, self-checks) happens inside build() on the warm model before validation; synchronization is a single default-stream replay per invocation with no extra streams, events, collectives or cross-rank transport (single-device task; rank 0 returns the local replacement and no collectives are required for participation).

steps: Load a tiny inline CUDA extension (two fused pointwise kernels: bn_relu, bn_add_relu) via torch.utils.cpp_extension.load_inline into /tmp/opop_resnet18_fused_v1; first build ~50s with nvcc, ~1s when the worker build cache is warm.

Fold the 20 frozen eval-mode BatchNorm2d modules once into per-channel scale=gammainvstd and shift=beta-meaninvscale float32 vectors (about 60 small tensors, <3KB total); model parameters are only read, never modified.
Run 3 warmup forwards of the fused callable on a side stream (settles cudnn heuristic plans with benchmark off, cublas workspaces and allocator blocks).
Capture the fused region forward into one CUDA graph on the live state['pixels'] storage; intermediates live in the graph private mempool.

Self-validate at build time: fused eager logits vs parent forward logits (gate 2e-5, falls back to a parent-identical eager mirror composed of the same module calls if violated), then replay vs eager fresh execution (gate 1e-5, falls back to uncaptured execution if violated).
setup_work.memory: Graph private mempool retains the region intermediates, on the order of 40-120MB on top of the resident model/activations; build-time peak briefly doubles the eager forward peak during warmup+capture. Per-timed-call peak_allocated_bytes drops (locally measured 323.6MB parent vs 118.2MB candidate) because replay performs no new allocations except the 128KB cloned logits.
setup_work.wall_clock_budget: about 50s cold (nvcc) or about 2s warm inside build(), plus one extra forward pair for self-validation; worker timeout is 600s.

quality_risks: Fused BatchNorm affine + ReLU and residual epilogue reorder floating-point rounding relative to aten batch_norm (fma-based, rsqrt-folded scale); locally observed max logit deviation 6.9e-06, far inside atol=rtol=1e-4, and top-1 identical; a 2e-5 build-time gate falls back to a bitwise parent-identical mirror if exceeded.

exact_top1 depends on logit perturbations staying below decision margins; perturbation is ~1e-5 on logits of magnitude up to ~15 with typical class margins far larger; still the canonical risk if the framework compares on different fixture slices - all fallbacks remain bitwise-identical to the parent.

CUDA graph replay returns the same kernels with the same arguments, so repeated replays are deterministic; if replay is rejected by the runtime (e.g. nested capture) the callable catches the error and uses the uncaptured fused path, and if the fused kernels were unavailable the parent bound forward is used.

Graph fast path is keyed on the exact observed (shape, stride, dtype, device, data_ptr) of state['pixels']; any other tensor (including clones) takes the eager fused path or the parent, so no stale-buffer or aliased-output semantics exist (each call returns a fresh clone).
Held-out unseen_batch (batch 7) and any kwargs variants execute the untouched parent forward, so coverage there is unoptimized but exact.
peak_allocated_bytes improves rather than regresses; the memory goal's images_per_second>=0.95x baseline constraint is therefore satisfied by construction as long as throughput improves.

usage.scope: Observed assistant message snapshots; provider estimates, not invoice
Observed assistant message snapshots; provider estimates, not invoice

external_invariants: Model is ResNetForImageClassification loaded from the local assets directory only (local_files_only=True) in float32; no downloads.
All weights and activations remain FP32; torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 and torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32 are False and torch.set_float32_matmul_precision('highest').
Seed policy: torch.manual_seed(20261020) applied in prepare, matching common.configure().

Input is the real preprocessed image fixture tensor from assets/pixels.npy (3 images, NCHW float32), selected as images[torch.arange(batch) % len(images)].contiguous(); for the frozen 'online' workload batch=1, i.e. the first image, unchanged every repeat.
The model is in eval() mode and the forward pass runs under torch.inference_mode(), identical to the source infer() helper calling model(pixel_values=pixels).logits.
Batch size is fixed at 1 for this workload; the workload, data, precision and output requirements are not altered to improve the score.
Correctness requires all logits within atol=1e-4 / rtol=1e-4 and exact top-1 argmax equality against the reference; observations include every logit and the predicted class integer.

Latency is wall time around run() with CUDA synchronization at both boundaries, per the source's per-repeat timing; throughput is derived from the unchanged work amount (batch=1) and the measured elapsed time.
The adapter does not initialize CUDA or load the model at import time and never destroys the process group in reset.
